subject: math
cluster: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples
description: Students fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation. They align decimal points for addition and subtraction, count and place decimal-point positions for multiplication, and shift the divisor and dividend to a whole-number divisor before dividing. They apply these procedures to multi-step and real-world money and measurement problems and check answers for reasonableness by estimation.
subSkills: Add multi-digit decimals by aligning decimal points and annexing zeros as placeholders
Subtract multi-digit decimals by aligning decimal points and regrouping across the decimal point
Multiply multi-digit decimals: multiply as whole numbers, then place the decimal point by counting total decimal places in the factors
Divide a decimal by a decimal by shifting both numbers so the divisor is a whole number, then dividing using the standard long-division algorithm
Divide where the quotient requires annexing trailing zeros to the dividend to continue or terminate
Estimate with rounding to check that a computed decimal answer is reasonable
Apply all four operations to multi-step real-world money and measurement contexts

problemArchetypes.name: Multi-step / real-world money problem
problemArchetypes.example: A shopper buys $3$ notebooks at $\$2.49$ each and pays with a $\$10$ bill. How much change is returned?

Easy.description: Single operation. Addition/subtraction with matching or one-off decimal places and no borrowing across the decimal point; multiplication with one factor a simple one-place decimal; division with a whole-number divisor that terminates quickly. Numbers are short (at most tenths or hundredths) and answers come out cleanly.
constraints: At most two decimal places in any operand
Addition/subtraction need at most one annexed zero and little or no regrouping across the decimal point
Division has a whole-number divisor and a terminating, short quotient
No estimation or reasonableness step required

Medium.description: Single operation but with the full standard algorithm in force: subtraction that regroups across the decimal point, multiplication where the decimal-point placement requires counting total places across both factors (including leading-zero results), or decimal-by-decimal division that requires shifting the point to make the divisor whole.
constraints: Operands may have up to three decimal places and unequal lengths (annex zeros)
Subtraction regroups across the decimal point; multiplication needs explicit place counting, possibly with a leading zero in the product (e.g. $0.\,\!\ldots$)
Division may require shifting both divisor and dividend so the divisor is a whole number
May ask the student to estimate first to place the point

Hard.description: Multi-step or contextual. Student parses a word problem, chooses and sequences two or more operations, may need to annex trailing zeros to finish a division, and verifies the answer by estimation. Includes comparison or unit-rate style follow-ups expressed with decimals.
constraints: Two or more operations sequenced, or a word problem requiring setup
Division may require annexing trailing zeros to the dividend to terminate, or interpreting a remainder in context
Mixes operations (e.g. multiply then subtract for change)
Requires a reasonableness/estimation check or a comparison between two decimal quantities

difficultyRubric.tierSplitGuidance: This standard uses a single ramped worksheet of 15 items (Easy early, Hard late). If split into two worksheets, tier1 covers Easy to Medium (one-operation fluency: aligned add/subtract, place-value multiplication, whole-number-divisor division) and tier2 covers Medium to Hard (decimal-by-decimal division with point shifting, annexing trailing zeros, and multi-step real-world money/measurement problems with estimation checks), with no item overlap.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Right-aligns the digits instead of aligning decimal points when adding or subtracting
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Treats $14.7 + 3.85$ as if it were $14.7 + 38.5$ or lines up last digits to get $14.92$ instead of $18.55$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Counts the decimal places of only one factor when placing the point in a product
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Computes $6.4 \times 0.25 = 16.0$ or $16$ instead of $1.6$ by using one decimal place rather than three total

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Forgets to annex a leading zero, mis-placing the decimal point in a small product
Shifts the decimal point in the divisor but not in the dividend (or shifts them by different amounts)
Drops or misplaces the decimal point in the quotient during long division
Stops dividing instead of annexing trailing zeros, leaving a remainder where a decimal answer is expected
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Reports $7.5 \div 4 = 1$ remainder $3.5$ or $1.5$ instead of continuing to $1.875$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Subtracts without regrouping across the decimal point, treating empty places as zero in the wrong direction
